/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report - 24 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3068 (68)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4942 (163)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2179 (30)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1811 (2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1077 (3)

CAPESIZE
The market continued to make gains today, with the Pacific once again leading the advance, supported by firm sentiment, active miner participation and solid operator demand. The North Atlantic was also showing signs of improvement, while the South Atlantic remained comparatively lacklustre. The BCI 182 5TC increased by $1,471 to $44,817. In the Pacific, the C5 index gained a further $0.407 to $16.085, with three miners active alongside solid operator demand. Offers opened around $17.00, following yesterday’s bullish close, against an operator bid of $15.65. As the day progressed, all three miners were reported fixing, with fixtures ranging between $15.90 and $16.00, while there was also talk of an operator paying $16.25. Overall sentiment remained firm, with the market continuing to find support from active demand. Conditions in the South Atlantic were rather less inspiring, with activity and sentiment lagging behind the Pacific. Nevertheless, the C3 index edged up by $0.255 to $35.191, with talk of a fixture at $35.25 for an 18 December onward date, suggesting some underlying optimism despite the lacklustre conditions. Further north, the North Atlantic was showing more encouraging signs, with sentiment turning increasingly positive and reports of stronger Transatlantic fixtures. The C8 index reflected this improvement, climbing $1,933 to $43,433.

PANAMAX
The Atlantic continued to support the market today with further gains reported from EC South America. Competition for tonnage throughout December was said to be underpinning sentiment, while recent fronthaul fixtures pointed to continued strengthening in rates. Although more owners were engaging in discussions market sources stated that the volume of outstanding enquiry appeared to be restricting charterers’ negotiating position. Firmer bidding was said to have emerged for mid-December trans-Atlantic requirements, despite activity for this route remaining relatively limited. The North Atlantic was described as less transparent, with rates largely dictated by vessel position and the urgency of individual requirements. Charterers appeared to have more tonnage options on the Continent, although suitable availability further south remained restricted and owners were described as generally reluctant to discount their offers. Festive-period redeliveries were also said to be shaping owners’ expectations. Meanwhile, the Pacific appeared to be gathering momentum as North Pacific enquiry increased alongside improving Australian demand. The additional cargo interest was helping to lift sentiment, with the P3A recording the strongest improvement on the day. Indonesia remained relatively steady, although the wider Pacific was beginning to show signs of strengthening, with owners becoming increasingly confident in their rate expectations. The P5TC increased by $268 to $19,611.

Atlantic
The Europa Graeca (82,043 2019) open Kandla 21 November was said to have been placed on subjects for an EC South America fronthaul with grains at $22,500 to Cargill. The Duchess Emerald (82,464 2024) open New Orleans 3 December was said to be on subjects, whilst the Velos Jade (80,679 2011) open Dunkirk 29/30 November was reported to have fixed a US East Coast trip to India, although no further details surfaced.

Asia
Tongli placed on subjects the Eastern Yucca (74,844 2012) open Xinsha 29 November for an Australian round trip at $16,250. Jera were said to have covered their stems from Indonesia for end-November dates, although no further details surfaced.

SUPRAMAX
Another indifferent day, with some marking the US Gulf up again, whilst others feel the market is more balanced going forward. The 11TC average was up slightly by $20 to close at $22,886. Sentiment in the South Atlantic remained positive with enough fresh enquiry to give Owners cause for optimism, the Continent continued to benefit from new scrap demand, whilst the Mediterranean still lacked any fresh impetus. In Asia the North seems to have found support with a few better fixtures being rumoured, while the South continues to suffer from ships ballasting from India/Bangladesh, giving Charterers the upper hand. The New Providence (63,911 2026) open Paradip 27 November-1 December was supposedly fixed for 2 laden legs at $21,000 basis scrubber for Charterers’ benefit, but no further details emerged.

HANDYSIZE
The market recorded a steady session, with rates holding up across most loading regions. The BHSI rose by 3 points to 1,077, while the 7TC average increased by $52 to close at $19,381. The Continent and Mediterranean remained broadly stable, supported by continued fresh demand. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic showed signs of losing momentum, with some sources reporting fewer prompt cargoes as the tonnage list began to lengthen. In contrast, activity in the US Gulf remained healthy, supported by a balanced tonnage list and strong underlying demand. The Pacific also held steady, with some sources highlighting tight prompt tonnage and healthy steel demand from China. The African Margaux (38,114 2020) open Kaohsiung on 26 November was reported fixed by Norden for a trip to the US Gulf in the $19,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
World Crude Steel Production

World crude steel production in October eased 1.1% year-on-year to 142.4 Mt, World Steel Association data show. Output fell in China (-1.6% to 70.8 Mt) and the EU (-1.7% to 14.3 Mt), with the Middle East reporting the largest regional decline, down 27.7% to 3.9 Mt. Conversely, North American production rose 6.0% to 8.4 Mt in October.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw a strong morning session before prices eased during the afternoon, with good activity across Dec, Q1 and Cal 27. Nov printed at 37,750, with limited activity. Dec opened at 37,000 before rallying to 37,900, Prices gradually weakened during the afternoon, falling to 37,300 before last trading at 37,400. THE INDEX HAS SHOWN A MILDLY POSITIVE MOVEMENT, WITH PACIFIC ROUTES BROADLY HOLDING FIRM, WHILE BUNKER PRICES REMAIN A FACTOR TO MONITOR. FFA PAPER HAS IMPROVED NOTABLY, SUGGESTING A BROADLY STABLE OUTLOOK FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE YEAR. WITH OWNERS BEGINNING TO PUSH OFFERS HIGHER, CHARTERERS MAY GRADUALLY NEED TO IMPROVE BIDS TO KEEP PACE, POTENTIALLY SETTING A FIRMER TONE FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE WEEK.
